title: granular-surge-shaping-sketch-azra
content:
Quick notes: idea = apply fine-grained per-tenant microthrottles + slot-smoothing to reduce p99 spikes during small, dense surges. Working sketch / lab log; not polished.

Background:
- Problem: short (~100-500ms) dense bursts from mobile clients produce p99 lat spikes despite healthy p50/p90. Batches overfill, KV cache thrashes, GPU kernels get small-batch overhead.
- Existing mitigations tried: global soft-rate limit, conservative batching, warm-path hints. Helps average but tail persists for multi-tenant pools.

Hypothesis:
1) If we keep small number of sticky "slots" (soft concurrency tokens) per tenant we can reduce inter-tenant interference during nanobursts.
2) Smooth slot release (exponential backoff-based damping) prevents synchronized release that causes sudden re-saturation.
3) Pairing with lightweight per-slot local queueing (max queue depth 4) keeps batch sizes reasonable without forcing cold dispatch to GPU.

Experiment setup (local lab):
- Model: open-llm-8b quantized (q4_0), typical seq=128 workload.
- Fleet: 4x A100 equiv nodes, each node runs 6 model workers.
- Baseline routing: round-robin across tenants, per-worker continuous batching (max_batch=32, timeout=8ms).
- New config: per-tenant slots=2, slot-hold-ttl=300ms, smooth-release-factor=0.7, local-queue-depth=4, max_batch=24, timeout=6ms.
- Workload: synthetic mixed-tenancy with 20 tenants, Zipf arrival, average qps 120 -> bursts up to 600 qps (over 2s windows). 30 minute runs.

Quick raw results (summary of one run):
- Baseline:
  * avg qps served: 118
  * GPU util: 72%
  * batch size mean: 18.7
  * latency p50/p90/p99: 22ms / 46ms / 312ms
  * KV cache hit rate: 67%
  * observed micro-tail events: 17 (events > 250ms)
- Granular-slot config:
  * avg qps served: 116 (small throughput loss)
  * GPU util: 68% (slightly lower but steadier)
  * batch size mean: 15.2 (less variance)
  * latency p50/p90/p99: 24ms / 49ms / 142ms
  * KV cache hit rate: 72% (improved local affinity)
  * observed micro-tail events: 4

Interpretation:
- p99 dropped ~55% (312 -> 142ms) with tiny throughput tradeoff. Many of the long tails in baseline were due to eviction/re-filling of per-worker KV cache when many tenants suddenly bunched requests on same worker. Slots created sticky locality so requests from the same tenant hit the same slot and benefitted from cached prefixes.
- Batch size variance decreased, which reduced kernel overheads for small batches. Fewer tiny batches dispatched.
- Smooth-release-factor helps avoid synchronized slot freeing (sawtooth). When factor tuned too low (<0.4) we observed queue backlog and p90 drift — need middle ground.

Observed pathologies / notes:
- Some tenants with very low sustained qps get starved during long sustained bursts because slots held by high-churn tenants. Mitigation: dynamic slot borrowing (not implemented yet) or slot decay faster for low-util tenants.
- When slot-hold-ttl too long (>=1s), fairness goes bad; too short (<100ms) loses cache affinity benefits. 300ms seemed a pragmatic middle for this workload.
- Edge case: multi-tenant requests with mixed sequence lengths create batch-fragmentation; need affinity-aware batch packing.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Run same config with real-client trace (NYC/EDGE) and a 24h run to measure diurnal effects.
- Implement adaptive slot counts per tenant (based on recent qps percentiles) and test fairness and SLOs.
- Evaluate slot-sharing across low-util tenants (soft pool) to avoid starvation.
- Measure memory/KV working set heatmaps per worker to confirm affinity hypothesis — capture sampled KV keys and overlap metrics.
- Try pairing with tiny-quantization variant on cold path to see if p99 can be further reduced with graceful fallbacks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should slot accounting be global to fleet or per-node? Tradeoffs: global harder to coordinate but may yield better utilization; per-node simpler and faster.
- How to surface slot-level telemetry in Console without noisy cardinality explosion? Proposed: sample 1% of slots and aggregate by tenant and worker.
- Interaction with Dedicated customers who pin variants: slot eviction policies need to respect tenancy SLAs.

Notes to self / ephemeral thoughts:
- Could graft slot idea onto existing per-tenant priority lane infra (reuse metrics, reuse quotas).
- For prototype, implement in runtime dispatcher as a thin layer that hands out concurrency tokens and local queue. Minimal risk: can be toggled via feature flag per pool.
- If this pattern works, productization path: give per-tenant "burst shaping" toggles in Console (default off for Dedicated).

Logs/attachments to save: upload raw run CSVs, flamegraphs, sampled traces. Will push to Confluence page and link here once available.

Immediate action items (short):
- [ ] convert synthetic runner to replay real mobile traces (Liam)
- [ ] prototype slot allocator in dispatcher (Maya)
- [ ] capture KV key overlap sampling script (Ravi)
- [ ] schedule 24h run next week and collect Console traces (me)

Unresolved: fairness definition for low-util tenants during extreme multi-tenant storms. Need policy discussion with SRE/product.

End-of-scratchpad.
